scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8873: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- the server farm and the other pod all time
out -- though it still pings its gateway 10.1.1.1 fine. Oddly, when we logged
into switch_dist_1_1 itself, the switch CAN ping the server farm. Pod 2 is
unaffected. Find what broke.

injection.action: remove the OSPF network statement that advertises the pod-1 host subnet

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_dist_1_1 OSPF configuration (missing
  `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` statement)
Mechanism: switch_dist_1_1 normally advertises the pod-1 host subnet
  10.1.1.0/24 into OSPF area 1; router_core_1 (the ABR) summarizes it into
  the area-0 backbone. With the network statement removed, the prefix is
  withdrawn everywhere, so the rest of the network loses its RETURN route to
  pod 1. The forward path still works -- switch_dist_1_1 keeps learning all
  remote routes over its uplink (172.16.0.6/31 is still in OSPF) -- so
  host_1_1_1_1's packets reach the farm and the replies are dropped on the
  way back: classic missing-advertisement asymmetry. switch_dist_1_1's own
  pings succeed because they source from its uplink address 172.16.0.7,
  which is still advertised.
Localization: switch_dist_1_1
Root cause: `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` removed from `router ospf` on
  switch_dist_1_1, so pod 1's subnet is no longer advertised
Fix: re-add the network statement on switch_dist_1_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
On switch_dist_1_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1"`
(`service frr restart` also heals it: the change was made only to the running
config, and /etc/frr/frr.conf still contains the statement.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The failure is in the routing control-plane on switch_dist_1_1 (FRR/OSPF). The L3 SVI/subnet for Pod 1 (10.1.1.0/24) is not being advertised into OSPF from switch_dist_1_1, so the rest of the network has no route back to hosts in that subnet. Evidence: switch_dist_1_1’s FRR config only advertises 172.16.0.6/31 (uplink) in OSPF (no “network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1”), while Pod 2’s switch_dist_2_1 correctly advertises 10.2.1.0/24. Consequently, switch_server_access (10.200.0.1) lacks a route to 10.1.1.0/24 (its routing table has no such entry) and returns ICMP Destination Net Unreachable when web servers or the DNS server try to reach 10.1.1.2. We captured these unreachables coming from 10.200.0.1. From host_1_1_1_1, pings to its gateway 10.1.1.1 succeed and traceroute shows the first hop (10.1.1.1) then timeouts, consistent with the return path being missing.

Affected component: FRR OSPF on switch_dist_1_1 (missing network statement). Mechanism: asymmetric routing—forward path from Pod 1 to servers exists, but reverse path is missing, causing timeouts and “net unreachable” from the server access switch. Localization: switch_dist_1_1, OSPF process; interface br0 (10.1.1.1/24) not in OSPF. Root cause: misconfiguration—10.1.1.0/24 not advertised into OSPF. Corrective fix: on switch_dist_1_1, add “network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1” under router ospf (or redistribute connected for br0), write/save config, and verify that 10.1.1.0/24 appears in the OSPF LSDB and routing tables on core and switch_server_access; then re-test ping from host_1_1_1_1 to 10.200.0.2.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names switch_dist_1_1 as the affected device and localizes the OSPF misconfiguration to it.

per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identified that switch_dist_1_1's FRR/OSPF is missing the 'network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1' statement, so the 10.1.1.0/24 subnet is not being advertised.

per_axis.rationale: The report notes the uplink (172.16.0.6/31) is advertised but does not explicitly explain that switch_dist_1_1’s own pings succeed because they source from the advertised uplink address (172.16.0.7).
Proposes adding the missing 'network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1' (or redistributing connected) on switch_dist_1_1 and saving/verifying, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log contains direct evidence (OSPF config lacking the 10.1.1.0/24 network on switch_dist_1_1, successful pings from pod to its gateway but timeouts/ICMP unreachable from the server-access switch, and switch_dist_1_1 having the subnet locally but not advertising it) that supports the asymmetric/missing-advertisement diagnosis. The inferences follow logically and the agent checked plausible alternative causes (firewall/ip-forwarding) and compared other devices' OSPF configs to localize the fault.
